mainTopic: How a dead נזיר's unassigned money goes to נדבה according to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and רבא's proof from the ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל that חטאת-related items cannot become other offerings.
overview: The משנה taught that if a נזיר set aside money without assigning it to specific offerings (סתומין) and then died, the money goes to voluntary offerings (נדבה). The גמרא asks how this can be, since part of that money was meant for a חטאת. רבי יוחנן answers that it is a special tradition (הלכה) for a נזיר. ריש לקיש learns it from a פסוק: the leftover of a vow becomes a נדבה. The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: by his reasoning, even assigned money (מפורשין) should go to נדבה. רבא answers with a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל. It teaches that the offspring and substitutes of קדשים are offered like the original animal, but the word ״רק״ leaves out the offspring of a חטאת and the substitute of an אשם. So money assigned to a חטאת cannot become a different offering. רבי עקיבא gives a different source for the אשם, ״אשם הוא״. The גמרא then looks closely at the ברייתא and asks why anyone would think these animals should be left to die. It begins to answer, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But the sin-offering money is mixed in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that a dead נזיר's unassigned money goes to voluntary offerings, since some of it was meant for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't the money for the sin-offering mixed in with these funds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling about a dead נזיר's unassigned money. Part of that money was supposed to buy a חטאת, so how can all of it become voluntary offerings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר brings three offerings: an עולה, a שלמים and a חטאת. Money meant for a חטאת whose owner died normally cannot be used for anything else. So it is surprising that the whole unassigned sum goes to נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Money set aside to buy a sin-offering
Mixed in
Unassigned money, not yet split between the specific offerings

phrases.english: But isn't the money of the sin-offering
phrases.notes: He means the share of the dead נזיר's money that was meant for his חטאת.

phrases.english: mixed in with them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling about סתומין money (taught before this section).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a dead נזיר's unassigned money falls to נדבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Part of the money belongs to a חטאת, and חטאת money cannot normally become a voluntary offering.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a special tradition for a nazir
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that this is a הלכה, a received tradition, that applies specifically to a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is an accepted tradition regarding a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. He says there is no logical source here: it is a received tradition that applies only to a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the rule comes from tradition and not from reasoning, it does not have to fit normal חטאת rules. It also applies only to exactly what the tradition says.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a received tradition (like הלכה למשה מסיני), not derived from a פסוק
A person who vowed to abstain from wine, haircuts and contact with the dead

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is a halakha concerning a nazir.
phrases.notes: Meaning a tradition handed down, not something learned from a פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה הִיא בְּנָזִיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special tradition overriding the usual rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חטאת money mixed into the funds should block using them for נדבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A received tradition rules that a נזיר's unassigned money goes to נדבה, despite the חטאת portion.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a vow's leftover becomes a gift offering
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the rule from a פסוק: whatever is left over from a vow is used for a voluntary offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says 'for all their vows and for all their gift offerings.' The תורה is teaching that the surplus of a vow should go to a voluntary offering.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different answer. He finds a source in the תורה: leftover money from a vow goes to voluntary offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'vows' (נדרים) right next to 'gift offerings' (נדבות). ריש לקיש reads this as saying that what is left of a נדר becomes a נדבה. Since the נזיר's vow can no longer be fulfilled, his money becomes a voluntary offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Their vows: offerings a person obligated himself to bring
Their gift offerings: voluntary offerings
The surplus or leftover of a vow
A voluntary offering

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
"For all their vows and for all their gift offerings,"
the Torah said:
the surplus of a vow shall be for a gift offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לְכׇל נִדְרֵיהֶם וּלְכׇל נִדְבוֹתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to step 1, parallel to רבי יוחנן's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חטאת portion should prevent the money from becoming נדבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה itself says a vow's leftover becomes a voluntary offering.

steps.title: Why only unassigned money according to ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's tradition can be limited to unassigned money, but ריש לקיש's פסוק seems to apply even to assigned money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי יוחנן, who says it is a tradition about a נזיר. That is why unassigned money goes to נדבה but assigned money does not. But for ריש לקיש, who learns it from 'for all their vows and for all their gift offerings,' why specifically unassigned money? Even assigned money should go to נדבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש. His פסוק seems to cover all vow money, so why does the משנה limit the rule to unassigned money?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, a tradition covers only what it says, which is unassigned money. But a פסוק about a vow's surplus seems to apply even when the money was already assigned to specific offerings (מפורשין). So the משנה's limit to סתומין is hard to explain for ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one opinion), setting up a challenge to the other
Because of this
Money already assigned to specific offerings
Why specifically this case?

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Yochanan,
who said: it is a halakha concerning a nazir,
because of this,
unassigned money, yes; assigned money, no.
But according to Reish Lakish,
"for all their vows and for all their gift offerings,"
why specifically unassigned money?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה הִיא בְּנָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both answers against the משנה's limit to סתומין and finds ריש לקיש's answer hard to fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's derivation from 'לכל נדריהם ולכל נדבותם'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general פסוק about a vow's surplus would cover assigned money too, but the משנה says only unassigned money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: רבא: assigned money is excluded by another teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבא defends ריש לקיש: assigned money cannot go to נדבה, because the school of רבי ישמעאל already ruled on a related matter about the offspring and substitutes of קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: you cannot say this about assigned money, because the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל already decided it: 'Only your holy things that you have, and your vows.' The פסוק is speaking about the offspring of sacred animals and their substitutes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge for ריש לקיש. He says assigned money is excluded by another source, and he starts quoting a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the פסוק 'רק קדשיך' is about animals that became holy only indirectly: the offspring (ולדות) of sacred animals and their substitutes (תמורה). רבא is bringing this teaching to show that some holy items have their own fixed rules and cannot simply become נדבה. The ברייתא continues in the next step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 on behalf of ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate source excludes assigned money
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's פסוק should make even assigned money go to נדבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל shows assigned money cannot be treated that way. Step 7 completes the link: ״רק״ leaves out the offspring of a חטאת.

steps.title: The remedy: bring them and actually offer them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: offspring and substitutes must be brought to the מקדש and actually sacrificed, not just left there to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is their remedy? 'You shall carry them and come to the place that ה׳ will choose.' One might think he brings them up to the מקדש and then withholds water and food from them so that they die. Therefore the פסוק says: 'And you shall offer your burnt-offerings, the flesh and the blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that רבא is quoting continues. It explains what to do with offspring and substitutes: bring them to the מקדש and actually offer them on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק only says to bring them to the מקדש, so one might think they are just brought there and left to die. The next פסוק, 'ועשית עולתיך הבשר והדם', shows they must actually be sacrificed. This sets up how רבא will use the ברייתא to answer the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Their remedy, what is done with them
The chosen house: the בית המקדש
One might have thought
Therefore the פסוק teaches

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree that a dead נזיר's unassigned money goes to נדבה. רבי יוחנן calls it a tradition, and ריש לקיש learns it from the פסוק 'the surplus of a vow goes to נדבה.' To defend ריש לקיש's limit to unassigned money, רבא quotes a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל. Its key point comes in the next step: ״רק״ excludes the offspring of a חטאת, so what comes from a חטאת cannot become another offering.

phrases.english: What is their remedy?

phrases.aramaic: ״תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה׳״.
phrases.english: "You shall carry and come to the place that the Lord will choose."
One might think he brings them up to the Temple,
and withholds water and food from them

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּקָּנָתָן תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה׳

steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל on דברים 12:26-27, about offspring and substitutes of קדשים.

steps.title: Offspring and substitutes follow the original offering, except for the חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that the substitute of an עולה and the offspring of שלמים are offered like the original animal. The word ״רק״ leaves out the offspring of a חטאת and the substitute of an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse comes to tell you: the way you treat an עולה, treat its substitute the same way. The way you treat שלמים, treat their offspring the same way. You might think the offspring of a חטאת and the substitute of an אשם are also offered. So the verse says ״רק״, which leaves them out. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It explains that substitutes and offspring are offered just like the original animal, but not when the original was a חטאת or an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״רק״ cuts out the offspring of a חטאת and the substitute of an אשם, so they are not offered. This proves that something that comes from a חטאת cannot become a different offering. That is exactly what רבא needs: money set aside for a חטאת cannot go to a נדבה, even according to ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן. It also becomes holy.
The offspring born to an animal that is a קרבן
A burnt-offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
A peace-offering. Parts go on the מזבח and the owners eat the rest.
"The verse says": it introduces the פסוק that proves the point
"Only": a word that limits the rule and leaves certain cases out

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the line that finishes רבא's proof. Leftover money assigned to a נזיר's חטאת cannot become a נדבה.

phrases.english: To tell you:
phrases.notes: The verse "ועשית עולותיך" from the end of the earlier line is coming to teach this.

treat their offspring.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף וְלַד חַטָּאת וּתְמוּרַת אָשָׁם כֵּן, —
phrases.english: You might think that the offspring of a sin-offering and the substitute of a guilt-offering are also like this,
so the verse says: "Only"
These are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לָךְ: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹהֵג בָּעוֹלָה

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's different source for the guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says there is no need to learn the אשם from ״רק״. The words ״אשם הוא״ already teach that only the original אשם is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: this is not needed. The verse already says ״אשם הוא״, "it is a guilt-offering". That means it, the original animal, stays as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees only about where the rule comes from. For the אשם, he points to a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״הוא״ ("it") means that only the original animal is offered as an אשם, not its substitute. So רבי עקיבא does not need ״רק״ to leave out the substitute of an אשם. Both תנאים agree on the result. They only argue about the source.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt-offering
"It is not needed": we don't need that source for this law
"In its being": in its own original state

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: It is not needed,
for it already says: "It is a guilt-offering"
It shall be in its own state.
phrases.notes: Only the original animal is offered as an אשם, not a substitute for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives a different source for the part of step 7 about the אשם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The substitute of an אשם is not offered, because ״אשם הוא״ means only the original animal is offered.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא agree that what comes from a חטאת or an אשם is not offered as a קרבן. That supports רבא's defense of ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא again: should these animals be left to die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to an earlier line of the ברייתא. That line asked whether these animals should be brought to the מקדש and starved to death. The verse ״ועשית עולותיך״ says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא taught: You might think you must bring them up to the מקדש and hold back water and food from them so that they die. So the verse says: "And you shall offer your burnt-offerings."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא again so it can look at it closely. This is a setup: the next step will question this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line was already part of the ברייתא in step 6. Now the גמרא repeats it with a new goal: to ask why anyone would even think of letting these animals die.

keyTerms.meaning: "It teaches": the גמרא is quoting the ברייתא
"The chosen house": the בית המקדש
"You might think": it introduces a wrong idea the verse will reject

phrases.english: It teaches: You might think he should bring them up to the Temple
phrases.notes: "Them" means the offspring and substitutes of קדשים from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and hold back water and food from them
so that they will die.
So the verse says: "And you shall offer your burnt-offerings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proof is finished. The גמרא now turns to look more closely at the ברייתא itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's line that the verse ״ועשית עולותיך״ rejects the idea of leaving these animals to die.

steps.title: Why would anyone think they should be left to die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא would even think of letting these animals die. We only learned that rule for the offspring of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would you think that? It is only the offspring of a חטאת that we learned must be left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's "you might think". The idea seems to have no basis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known tradition that the offspring of a חטאת is left to die. But nobody ever said that about the offspring of other offerings or about substitutes. So why would we need a verse to reject that idea for them?

keyTerms.meaning: "Why?": a challenge to the reasoning
"We learned": a rule we have from a received tradition
Death: here, leaving the animal to die

phrases.english: Why? It is the offspring of a sin-offering
that we learned about it that it is left to die!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? הָא וְלַד חַטָּאת הוּא דִּגְמִירִין בָּהּ מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the "you might think" of the line quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's idea that other offspring and substitutes might be left to die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of being left to die was taught only for the offspring of a חטאת. So there is no reason to think it applies to others, and no need for a verse to reject it.

steps.title: Without the verse, we would have made a mistake about the offspring of a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer. Without the verse, we would have said that the offspring of a חטאת can be left to die anywhere. The answer continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the verse, I would have said that the offspring of a חטאת may be left to die anywhere,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining why the ברייתא needed the verse. The answer is still in the middle and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer starts by saying what we would have thought about the offspring of a חטאת without the verse: that it can be left to die anywhere, not only in the מקדש. The rest of the answer, explaining how this leads to the ברייתא's "you might think", comes next.
